rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track, with progress 0.11 to 0.18 (about 0.5 to 0.8 m of a 4 to 5 m course). Max error reached about 0.06 m in every trial, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 for any allowed body width). RMS error was about 0.02 to 0.03 m. Iteration 1 (base 1.2, sensors at y=0.05, kp 2.0, kd 0.6) was not better than iteration 0 (base 1.5, y=0.03, kp 2.5, kd 0.2): mean scores fell from 59.9 to 58.2, and progress on the s-bend and oval changed little. So the lower speed, the extra lead and the extra damping did not fix the problem. Line loss happened once per trial in iteration 0, which suggests the line leaves the sensor array at the edge of its span, not that the robot is too fast. The sensors span only x = -0.04 to +0.04. Once the tape centre is about 0.05 m off the centre line, the tape falls outside the array and the robot has to recover blind. Changes: (1) Widen the sensor span to x = -0.06 to +0.06 with 5 sensors, and enlarge the sensor footprint to 16 mm so the 25 mm tape is always covered by at least one sensor. (2) Keep the sensors at y=0.05, which the iteration-1 evidence did not show to hurt. (3) Raise kp from 2.0 to 3.0. The wider spacing lowers the signal gain per metre of offset (about 33 per m instead of 50 per m), so a higher kp keeps the steering authority similar. (4) Set kd to 0.4, between the two earlier values, to damp without over-filtering. (5) Set base_speed to 1.3, between the 1.2 and 1.5 that were tried, to keep average speed near the level needed to finish. Geometry is otherwise unchanged. Expected result: fewer or no line-loss events, max error held below 0.06 m, and progress rising above about 0.25 on the development tracks. Finishing within 3 s is still uncertain. The telemetry should show whether the wider span fixes the early drift.
